identityReview: Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim, also Hindou Ibrahim, Chadian Indigenous-rights and climate advocate from the Mbororo/Fulani pastoralist community. UNESCO supports birth in 1984; the 2015 journal interview supports N’Djamena. Retain year-only birth precision. Contemporary September/November 2026 sources identify AFPAT president. Her 2024 UN Permanent Forum chairmanship belongs to the twenty-third session; the 2026 chair is Aluki Kotierk. SDG Advocate, Conservation International fellow, civil-society speaker and award recipient are distinct roles, not governmental authority or proof of an academic degree.
lifeStatusEvidence: The Prince Albert II Foundation’s 17 October 2026 report explicitly records the 16 October award ceremony, names Ibrahim as the Awareness laureate and says the laureates accepted their awards. The 23 September UN transcript additionally records her introduced intervention; the 9 November bylined SDG Action article is further recent authorship/role evidence. No image or recording is claimed to have been visually or aurally checked.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read UNESCO and 2015 interview passages, UN Partnerships biography, relevant IISD 2016 ceremony passages, concise IISD 2019 appointment report, UCLA award article, selected final UN 2024 report paragraphs, the 2026 chair statement heading/introduction, Monaco award release, November article and the relevant UN transcript segment. Rolex award/profile details were read as indexed excerpts because legacy pages redirected. Read Commons metadata/licence/history without photo pixels.
corrections: Read the UNESCO Courier interview published 15 January 2019, later updated 27 April 2023. Its biographical paragraph explicitly gives 1984 in Chad, and the interview separates AFPAT creation in 1999 from legal status in 2005. No January 1 birthday is inferred from year-only data. It discusses rights, education, health, justice, women’s participation and environmental knowledge. Her descriptions of gains and deficiencies are interview testimony, not a fresh 2026 legal audit. The old reference to Idriss Déby as current president is historical; neither this office nor other 2019 conditions are carried forward as current.

Read the 2015 Pollution atmosphérique interview’s introduction and formation-history answer. It supports N’Djamena birthplace, Mbororo/Fulani identity, her mother’s support for schooling, 1999 creation and 2005 operating permission. Sources elsewhere describe activism beginning at 12, association creation at 15 or 16, and one indexed later interview collection gives 2006 recognition; do not force these into one certain age/date sequence. The timeline attributes 2005 to the two directly read interviews, not to an inspected registration certificate. Introductory generalisations about girls’ marriage or literacy are not applied to every Mbororo woman or to all Indigenous peoples.

Read the UN Office for Partnerships profile, including the fuller biography. It supports AFPAT founding/leadership, community-based mapping, work across climate/biodiversity/desertification discussions and senior Indigenous fellowship at Conservation International since 2018. The page alternates present and past tense for international climate-forum co-chairmanship; no unrefreshed current claim for that office is adopted. Its National Geographic Explorer recognition is not a geography degree or university appointment. The 2018 fellowship is an institutional role; no unverified degree or exact appointment month is invented.

Read the relevant opening/location and Ibrahim intervention passages of IISD Earth Negotiations Bulletin’s 22 April 2016 report. It confirms actual speech at UN Headquarters, New York, as a civil-society representative, with adaptation-finance and climate-impact concerns. The Paris name belongs to the agreement, not the location of this signing event. She was not thereby Chad’s state signatory, a head of state, or sole author of the treaty. A preparatory UN press notice alone would be prospective; this contemporaneous report supplies the completed-event evidence. No complete recording or all national speeches were reviewed.

Read the concise IISD SDG Knowledge Hub report: 9 May 2019, six new advocates including Ibrahim, taking the group to 17. The public text distinguishes the number newly appointed from the full group. SDG advocacy is not an administrative headship of the UN Secretariat or national executive office. The named co-chairs and other members in this 2019 article are historical; their present positions are not inferred. UN primary announcement/briefing bodies were inaccessible, while their indexed dates and appointment snippets corroborate the readable report.

Read UCLA’s 8 November 2019 report. It explicitly places the award ceremony on 7 November at Hershey Hall, gives US$100000 and identifies the Pritzker Emerging Environmental Genius Award. It is not the architecture prize, and the 8 November publication date is not the ceremony date. Mapping methods are described as gathering resource knowledge from multiple local groups; reports of reduced tension are project accounts, not an independent impact experiment. Its 90 percent Lake Chad decline since 1980 differs from later sources’ 1960s baseline and was omitted. Its prospective 2020 Glasgow event is not proof of a conference subsequently occurring on that schedule.

Read the indexed Rolex laureate profile and indexed five-winners announcement. They identify a 2021 award for combining Indigenous knowledge with natural-resource mapping and climate adaptation. The profile says published November 2022, while the indexed jury account describes selection in November 2020; neither replaces the 2021 award year. Opening these legacy Rolex pages redirected to current general watch/newsroom pages, so no claim is made to have read their recovered full bodies. No grant amount, exact announcement day or independently proven conflict-prevention outcome is asserted.

Read the relevant organisation-of-session and bureau-election paragraphs of final UN report E/2024/43–E/C.19/2024/8. Paragraph 164 dates the first meeting to 15 April 2024 and paragraph 167 identifies Ibrahim as elected chair, with Aluki Kotierk among the vice-chairs. This establishes the twenty-third-session chairmanship, not a permanent office or an unlimited mandate. No claim to have read all recommendations or all pages of the report is made.

Read the heading and introductory report-presentation passage of the ECOSOC statement dated 21–22 July 2026. It identifies chair Aluki Kotierk and the twenty-fifth Forum session held 20 April–1 May 2026. This prevents carrying Ibrahim’s 2024 chair title forward as the current 2026 chair. It does not by itself establish Ibrahim’s exact last day in office, every intervening chair election, or whether she retained another Forum membership; no such dates or claims are invented.

Read the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation’s 17 October 2026 release: ceremony on Friday 16 October, named laureates and acceptance of awards. Ibrahim’s category is Awareness for Indigenous rights and traditional ecological knowledge, distinct from David Obura’s Science award and CorPower Ocean’s Innovation and Solutions award. No coral-reef research, wave-energy invention, projected electricity output or IPBES chairmanship is attributed to her. The report documents a completed award reception, not simply nomination or a future invitation; no photo pixels or ceremony video were reviewed.

Read the 9 November 2026 bylined SDG Action article, author role, and sections on land rights, participatory mapping, cross-border cooperation and direct local finance. It identifies her as AFPAT president and supplies recent authorship evidence, not independent proof of an in-person event. The policy prescriptions and claims about project effects remain attributed. No independent audit of all project outcomes, climate-finance percentages or Lake Chad surface-area estimates was performed; the 90-percent statistic and population counts were not imported. Its age-12 activism shorthand does not change the 1999 association date or prove foundation at age 12.

Read the UN transcript page heading dated 23 September 2026 and the moderator introduction and Ibrahim intervention around 4:54:25. It names her as an SDG Advocate and AFPAT president and records discussion of knowledge, decision-making power, resources and community consent. It is a transcript preview with apparent transcription errors, not a verified verbatim edition; no audio/video was reviewed. The dossier paraphrases broad themes rather than reproducing uncertain wording or transferring other speakers’ statistics and statements to her. This supports recent public activity separately from the November byline.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified native-language human review. No birth certificate, AFPAT registration document, academic credential, complete Forum report, full project-impact evaluation, hydrological time series, financial audit, video/audio recording or portrait pixels were reviewed. Leave birth month/day unspecified; do not resolve conflicting activism ages or 2005/2006 registration accounts by invention. Preserve attribution of policy proposals and organisational outcomes. Refresh current roles and recent events before publication.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed against Chinese and English. Preserve year-only 1984 birth and N’Djamena; Mbororo/Fulani community identity; 1999 creation versus interview-attributed 2005 legal status; 2016 New York civil-society speech versus state signature; 2018 institutional fellowship versus degree; six new advocates versus 17 total in 2019; 7 November award versus 8 November report and environmental prize versus architecture prize; 2021 Rolex award versus jury/profile dates; 2024 session chair versus Kotierk’s 2026 role; 16 October 2026 Awareness award versus next-day release and other laureates’ achievements; attributed mapping/climate-finance claims versus independent impact findings.
